data.probe: Finding mixes two claims, both false. (1) Path traversal: current ddflow/services/recovery.py:183 already uses W.load_path(repo, worktree), not Path(repo)/worktree — fixed by commit 350f28650 'Resolve worktree path via W.load_path in the base_ref repair (absolute paths)'. (2) base_ref='' is not an error: the knob default IS '' and its doc says 'Empty means auto-detect the default branch (origin/HEAD, else main, else master)'; every consumer uses cfg.worktree.base_ref or W.default_branch(...). Resetting a stale flag to '' is the documented auto-detect default, exactly what _repair_base_ref's docstring intends.
data.title: ddflow/services/recovery.py:183

chunk_findings.detail: The apply path rewrites the first `base_ref = "..."` line in the whole file and treats that as success, without requiring a `[worktree]` table or a value that still starts with `-`. Given `.ddflow/config.toml` containing an earlier `base_ref = "main"` (another table, or `worktree.base_ref` is not how the line is spelled) and `[worktree]\nbase_ref = "--local"`, detection still sets `stale_base_ref` from the parsed `[worktree]` key, but `re.subn(..., count=1)` blanks the first assignment, returns `applied: True`, and leaves `base_ref = "--local"`. The next `recover --apply` matches the already-rewritten first line again, so the InvalidValue never clears.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/recovery.py:_repair_base_ref

chunk_findings.detail: Repair is skipped for any item already in `capped`, because `continue` runs before the `stale_base_ref` branch. An expired-lease (or other capped) worktree whose local config is still `base_ref = "--local"` and whose attempt count is already `>= max_attempts` gets only the cap action, never `repair_base_ref`. `gate status` / `claim` still raise `InvalidValue: invalid worktree.base_ref = --local`, which is the failure this change claims to repair for every salvage verdict.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/recovery_plan.py:_recovery_actions

chunk_findings.detail: The regression that is supposed to close Bda0ba7b9eb only checks that the string `--local` is gone from the worktree config after `recover --apply`. It never checks that `worktree.base_ref` was rewritten to a usable ref (the bug required `main`) or that `claim`/`status` no longer raise `InvalidValue`. Given a repair that deletes the line, writes `base_ref = ""`, or writes another flag such as `--branch`, `(wt / ".ddflow" / "config.toml").read_text()` still does not contain `--local`, so the test passes while gate status/claim still fail exactly as before the fix. The unit case is the same shape: it asserts the command string and `SAFE_AUTO`, and only for `salvageable=False`, so a planner that skips the repair when the orphan is salvageable also goes uncaught despite the docstring claiming every salvage verdict.
